goals: Display a visually distinct "About Me" section on the home page with the author's identity.
Reuse the existing `GIST_ACCOUNT` config variable as the source of truth for the GitHub username.
Prefer rich Markdown content (profile README) over structured profile fields when available.

userStories.title: Author can see the About Me section rendered on the home page
userStories.description: As a blog author, I want an "About Me" section to appear on the home page so that visitors immediately know who I am.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The home page (`/`) renders an "About Me" section above or below the post list.
The section renders content from the profile README if available, or falls back to the account profile fields (avatar, name, bio, location, website) if not.
If neither source yields any content, the section is omitted entirely — the page does not break.

userStories.title: About Me content is read from the GitHub profile README.md
userStories.description: As a blog author, I want my GitHub profile README to be the primary source of my About Me content so that I manage everything from my GitHub profile page.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The feature reads the username from `GIST_ACCOUNT` (exported from `config/gist.ts`); no username is hardcoded.
The fetcher attempts to retrieve the raw `README.md` from the special profile repository: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{username}/{username}/HEAD/README.md`.
If the README.md exists (HTTP 200), its Markdown content is rendered in the About Me section.
The rendered Markdown is sanitized before display (no raw HTML injection).
Fetching happens server-side so no credentials are exposed to the client.
Visually verified in browser with a username that has a profile README.

userStories.title: About Me falls back to GitHub account profile when no README exists
userStories.description: As a blog author without a GitHub profile README, I want the About Me section to still show my account information so that the section is never empty for visitors.

acceptanceCriteria.text: If the README.md request returns a non-200 status (e.g. 404), the fetcher falls back to calling `https://api.github.com/users/{username}`.
The fallback renders at minimum: avatar image and display name.
Optional fields shown when present: bio, location, blog/website URL (as a clickable link).
If the GitHub Users API also fails, the section is omitted gracefully — no error is shown to the visitor.

functionalRequirements.description: The feature reads the username exclusively from `GIST_ACCOUNT` (exported by `config/gist.ts`).

A server-side function `fetchProfileReadme(username: string): Promise<string | null>` fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{username}/{username}/HEAD/README.md` and returns the raw Markdown string on HTTP 200, or `null` otherwise.

A server-side function `fetchGitHubProfile(username: string): Promise<GitHubProfile | null>` fetches `https://api.github.com/users/{username}` and returns the mapped profile object on success, or `null` on any failure.
A `GitHubProfile` type defines the shape: `{ avatarUrl: string; name: string | null; bio: string | null; location: string | null; website: string | null }`.

The orchestrating logic tries `fetchProfileReadme` first. If it returns a non-null string, that Markdown is passed to the `AboutMe` component as the primary content. Otherwise, `fetchGitHubProfile` is called and its result is passed as the fallback content.
An `AboutMe` React Server Component accepts either `{ mode: "readme"; markdown: string }` or `{ mode: "profile"; profile: GitHubProfile }` and renders accordingly.
In `"readme"` mode, the Markdown is rendered using the existing Markdown renderer (e.g. `react-markdown`) with sanitization.
In `"profile"` mode, the avatar image uses `next/image` with appropriate `alt` text (author's name or `"Author avatar"`).
If both sources return `null`, `AboutMe` is not rendered and the home page shows only the post list.
All network calls are server-side only (Next.js Server Component or equivalent).
